source.title: Sparse Autoencoders for Expert-Assisted Interpretation of Histopathology Foundation Model Embeddings

record.tranche_reason: Applies SAE feature recovery and characterization to histopathology foundation-model embeddings, an application setting distinct from toy networks and language models.
record.gate_note: Tests whether sparse dictionary features can be recovered and characterized in real foundation-model embeddings. The study does not test toy-model superposition, feature-capacity competition, or neural polysemanticity. SAE comparisons, label-enrichment statistics, and downstream class-signal results are recorded; reconstruction model-selection figures and results cited from other studies are not claim-specific rows.
record.test_reason: Trains SAEs on two pathology vision foundation models (CONCH, UNI2-h) and measures whether recovered sparse features are more coherent and label-concentrated than raw dimensions, PCA or random directions. This is a new setting (vision embeddings, not LLMs) for V4's dictionary-recovery claim. It does not test toy-model geometry, capacity, or feature canonicity.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that SAEs make parts of pathology foundation-model embedding spaces more inspectable, with coherent, label-enriched latents and preserved class information, consistent across CONCH and UNI2-h. Latents are to be treated as candidate concepts needing pathologist assessment. They also state that raw dimensions and PCA remain competitive for classification.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains overcomplete sparse autoencoders on fixed foundation-model embeddings and characterizes their learned features. It does not reproduce the toy-network construction or feature-geometry experiments of the cited original source.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported retrieval comparison depends on signed-direction tail handling: best-tail baselines narrow the CONCH coherence gap. Feature behavior also differs between CONCH and UNI2-h; UNI2-h has lower reported SAE retrieval coherence and label concentration values, while still outperforming its listed direction baselines.

fits_no_version.finding: Low dictionary utilization: only 685/4096 (16.7%) CONCH SAE latents ever activate, versus 73% alive for UNI2-h. Wider dictionaries reconstruct better but use fewer latents.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE dictionary utilization on narrow-domain embeddings is low and backbone-dependent, so many learned latents are dead.

record.problems: The main analysis uses one dataset, with limited foundation-model coverage. There is no systematic pathologist evaluation, feature stability across datasets is not established, and analyses are correlational rather than causal. Some qualitative features are mixed or ambiguous.
record.rows_left_out: No results left out under the 60-row limit. SAE model-selection reconstruction comparisons and additional sparsity/reconstruction ablations were not recorded because they do not directly measure the claim versions.

untested.parts: LLMs (only vision pathology embeddings tested). Whether features are spread across many neurons is not directly measured beyond signed raw-dimension retrieval.
All: no toy models, sparsity transition, or geometry.
All: no capacity or importance analysis.
Completeness, stability across seeds or datasets at the feature level, and canonicity are not tested. Mixed or ambiguous features are shown only qualitatively (Fig. 9).

missing.what: UNI2-h vs CONCH SAE reconstruction fidelity: NMSE 0.167 vs 0.012, EV 0.798 vs 0.978, alive 73% vs 13%
Selected raw-dimension probe baseline matching selected SAE features (k=1: 0.873 vs 0.858; k=3: 0.927 vs 0.921; k=10: 0.936 both)
Top-16/top-64 retrieval sensitivity: SAE advantage holds (e.g., top-64 SAE 0.822 vs raw 0.430)

record.verdict_notes: The V5 label was dropped: the study does not test completeness, stability or canonicity of features, and r37 does not measure V5. Comparator and control rows were re-stated as the size of the SAE advantage. The setting is vision pathology embeddings rather than LLMs, so V4 verdicts apply only to that setting.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks, more sparse features than dimensions, overlapping near-orthogonal directions, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Whether neuron polysemanticity results from capacity competition or whether importance determines dedicated versus shared dimensions.
Whether polysemantic neurons arise for reasons other than capacity pressure.
The study concerns pathology foundation-model embeddings, not LLMs; it does not establish that features are spread across many neurons in LLMs.
It does not establish feature completeness, stability across datasets or training runs, or canonical status; systematic pathologist validation is absent.
Whether the underlying model features are intrinsically one-dimensional rather than multidimensional.

relation.reason: Reports feature sparsity, label enrichment and controlled retrieval comparisons bearing on V4's recoverability claim in this new setting.

tranche.reason: Tests dictionary-recovered sparse structure in a new setting: pathology vision embeddings from CONCH and UNI2-h.

source_check.notes: This is an extension to vision embeddings, not a direct LLM test; the authors report correlational candidate concepts without systematic pathologist validation. Table 9 reports probe standard deviations omitted from the pack's uncertainty fields.

statements.correction: Table 9, k=3: selected raw dimensions macro-F1 0.927 ± 0.002; selected SAE features 0.921 ± 0.002. Section 4.5: raw dimensions and PCA remain competitive; sparse SAE representations preserve and partially concentrate class information.
statements.problem: The pathology comparison is accurate, but its limits_scope framing exceeds V4: V4 does not require SAE-specific class-signal concentration or classifier superiority.
